Allow.description: What a replacement may change besides adding declarations.

AtPosition.description:
What Lean recorded at a position asked about in `at`. Each part is
absent when no syntax of its kind written in the code contains the
position; the innermost one is reported, the range that starts last,
then ends first.

tactic.description: The tactic at the position, with the goals before and after it.

term.description:
With `detail: ["terms"]`, the term at the position that Lean
elaborated against an expected type. Lean gives the head of an
application the application's: on `f` in `f x`, this is `f`,
expecting what `f x` was expected to be.

entry.description:
An entry on the module that declares it: one with the labels if there
is one.

signature.description: As written, from its module's declaration export.

used_by.description: The entries' declarations that rest on it.

verified.description: Its module has passed the kernel re-check.

AuditSummary.description:
The entries' declarations by status, each module's once, without the
assumptions themselves and what Lean generated.

unverified_modules.description:
The entries' modules that haven't passed the kernel re-check, so
whose statuses come from the build's report.

axioms.description: Its axioms outside the allowed list.

items.description: The code to check; each item gets a result, in this order.

at.description: Up to 64 positions in the code to report on: [`CheckResult::at`].

version.description: Worker pool label or alias; defaults to the server's default.

at.description: With `at`, what Lean recorded at each position, in request order.

declarations.description: Declarations the code added, with the axioms each depends on.

error.description: Why the check could not complete (timeout, crash, policy, ...).

messages.description: Lean's messages, with positions in the submitted code.

ok.description:
True when the code elaborated without errors and passed every policy
check: only standard axioms, no metaprogramming, allowed options, and
for session checks, the session's original statements.

reasons.description: Why `ok` is false, e.g. "axiom: t uses sorryAx".

tactics.description:
With `detail: ["tactics"]`, one entry each time a tactic in the code
ran, in the order Lean ran them. A tactic run on several goals, as
under `all_goals` or `<;>`, appears once per run, and so does every
alternative `first` tried.

time.description: Seconds Lean spent on the code.

deps.description: Declarations it uses, in its statement and its proof or body.

type_full.description: The type with full names and no notation.

used_by.description: Declarations that use it, most prominent first (at most 50).

Declaration.description: A new declaration and the axioms it depends on.

assumes.description:
Its axioms that are assumptions: declared as `axiom` in this code or
in a snapshot it builds on. Absent in records from before they were
reported.

generated.description:
Made by Lean on demand, such as an equation lemma: code with the same
statements needn't have it.

status.description: What its axioms make it, by [`ProofStatus`].

type_hash.description:
A hash of its type, with private names taken without their module,
and with the internal auxiliaries it uses folded in.

type_refs.description:
The constants of this code and of the snapshots it builds on that its
type uses, through internal auxiliaries. Absent in records from before
they were reported.

value_hash.description:
For definitions, a hash of the value, as of the type, so a proof can't
change what a statement means by redefining something it mentions.

value_refs.description:
The same for a definition's value, or an inductive's constructors and
recursor.

Deleted.description:
`DELETE /snapshots/{entry}`: deletes the entry. Its module goes too once
no entry and no kept module needs it, and then so do the modules it
imports, on the same terms.

removed.description: The modules removed, the entry's own first.

Detail.description: Extra detail a check can return, requested in `detail`.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

additive_sibling.description: The `to_additive` counterpart, folded into this hit.

imports.description:
The import header that loads it, when the index's default header
(`import Mathlib` and `import Physlib`) doesn't.

informal.description: A Physlib informal result: stated, not proved.

uses_sorry.description: Depends on `sorry`: not usable as a proof step.

Health.description: `GET /health`: 200, or 503 once the server is stopping.

oneOf.description: Search's state; `null` if the server doesn't search.

status.description: `draining`, with a 503, once the server is stopping.

workers.description: The live workers on the queue; `null` if it can't be read.

score.description: Fused score; only comparable within one query.

snapshot.description:
For a declaration of a snapshot module (named in `module`, with the
header that loads it in `flags.imports`).

summary.description: One or two sentences describing it, when a description exists.

text.description: About 150 tokens for a model's context.

Informal.description: A natural-language description of a declaration.

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. "lsv2-v4.28.0-rc1" or a model name.

JobKind.description: The endpoint an async request ran.

JobOutcome.description:
What `GET /jobs/{job}` answers once the job is done: what its request
would have. By `kind`: `check` and `check_session` a `CheckResult`,
`start_session` a `StartResponse`, `tactic` a `TacticResponse`,
`create_snapshot` a `SnapshotResponse`, `verify_snapshot` a
`SnapshotVerified` and `rebuild_snapshots` a `RebuildResponse`. An error
is the request's own, with its status.

JobStatus.description: An async request, as `/jobs/{job}` reports it until it is done.

job.description:
Its id: 32 hex digits, to keep secret, as anyone who has it can read
the answer or cancel the job.

LabelsRequest.description:
`PATCH /snapshots/{entry}`: removes the labels `remove` names, then sets
those in `set`. The labels that result must follow the rules of
[`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels).

ModuleDecl.description:
A declaration of a snapshot module, with its description once search has
written one (with `PISA_SEARCH_DESCRIBE_MODEL`).

Pos.description:
A position in the submitted code: lines count from 1, and columns from 0
in Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units.

ProofStatus.description:
What a declaration's axioms make it, besides the allowed ones (by default
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`), worst last.

Query.description:
One search. Fill as many fields as you can: each feeds different lanes,
and more fields mean better fusion.

goal.description: A pretty-printed goal state (hypotheses and `⊢ target`).

include_sorried.description: Also return declarations that depend on `sorry`, flagged.

latex.description: The statement in LaTeX, e.g. `S(\rho_{AB}) \le S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B)`.

name.description: A declaration name, possibly partial or misspelled.

pattern.description: A Lean expression or pattern, e.g. `Matrix.trace ?A = 1`.

q.description: Free text from a person; classified as natural language, LaTeX, Lean or a name.

snapshots.description: Snapshots to search as well as the base libraries (default: none).

verify.description: Check hits against `goal` on a Lean worker (not available yet).

dense_pending.description:
The dense lane was left out because the query is still being
embedded; asking again shortly will likely include it.

verification.description: Set when `verify` was asked for, e.g. "unavailable".

warnings.description: What made this result worse than usual, e.g. a lane that failed.

result.description:
The create's check: Lean's errors, a refused replacement's
`reasons`, or the `error` that stopped it.

RebuildItem.description:
A create in a [`RebuildResponse`]: `POST /snapshots` with its `code`, `labels`
and `key`.

affected.description:
The theorems of the module whose type uses a changed definition,
directly or through other definitions, here or below.

affected_unknown.description:
Which theorems use a changed definition is unknown: this module, or
one it builds on in the plan, has no declaration export to read.

code.description: The old module's code with its imports swapped.

entry.description:
The entry it rebuilds. Absent for a module that only links others to
`from`, with no entry that has the labels: it gets the labels asked
for.

key.description:
The idempotency key to create it with. Planning again gives the same
keys, so running a plan again after a failure replays the creates
that are done.

level.description:
1 for a module that imports `from`'s, 2 for one that imports that, and
so on, by its longest chain.

new_header.description: The header of code on top of the new module.

replaces.description:
When `to` replaces `from`, the entry it rebuilds, to create it as a
replacement of, with the same `allow`. The create then checks that
nothing its statements depend on changed, and is refused if
something did.

RebuildRequest.description:
`POST /snapshots/rebuild`: plans how to create the dependents of `from`
(see [`SnapshotDependents`]) again on `to`, each with its imports of
`from`'s module, and of the other modules it rebuilds, swapped for the new
ones, and unless `dry_run` creates them: a level at a time, a level's
creates side by side once the level below is done.

allow_changes.description:
Plan even though `to` changes what `from` states, when `to` wasn't
created to [`replace`](SnapshotRequest::replaces) `from`.

dry_run.description: Only plan: the client creates the plan's items.

labels.description:
Which dependents to rebuild: those with an entry that has every label,
and the modules they build on above `from`. Required, so that the
caller chooses which projects follow the edit.

retire.description:
Once every item is created, delete the old entries, from the top
down, then `from`, and with them the old modules nothing else needs.

RebuildResponse.description:
What a rebuild planned and, unless it was a dry run, did. Sending the same
rebuild again plans the same items with the same keys, so the creates that
are done replay their entries, and the rest run.

changes.description:
How `to` differs from `from`, as in a refused replacement's
`result.reasons`. Empty when `to` replaces `from`: its create
compared them.

created.description: For a run, the items created, in plan order.

failed.description: For a run, the items whose create kept nothing.

ok.description:
For a plan, whether there is one: false when `to` changes what `from`
states and `allow_changes` isn't set. For a run, whether every item
was created, and retired if asked.

plan.description:
The creates to make, by level, then oldest first. A level's items can
be created together once the level below is done.

retired.description: With `retire`, the old entries deleted, top down, `from` last.

skipped.description:
For a run, the items not created because they build on one that
failed or was skipped. Other branches go on.

RebuildSkipped.description: A [`RebuildItem`] not created, because it builds on one that wasn't.

Replaced.description: An entry that another replaced, and how.

Replacement.description:
[`SnapshotResponse::replaces`]: the entry the create replaced, and what
the replacement changed.

affected.description:
The theorems whose type uses a changed definition, directly or
through another definition.

changed_definitions.description: With `allow: "definitions"`, the definitions whose value changed.

filled.description:
The replaced module's declarations that used `sorry` and no longer
do. Empty on a key replay, which doesn't compare again.

Replaces.description: [`SnapshotRequest::replaces`]: an entry, or an entry and what may change.

deprecated_to.description: For a deprecated name, its replacement.

suggestions.description: Closest existing names, best first; empty for an exact match.

error.description: Why the index isn't open yet.

leader.description: This replica leads the snapshot index.

ready.description: The index is open and Qdrant answers, so searches can be served.

env_id.description: Fails with `not_found` unless the server has this environment.

SessionCheckRequest.description:
`POST /sessions/{session}/check`: re-checks completed code from scratch
and confirms it proves the statements the session started from, with the
same imports.

SnapshotAudit.description:
`GET /snapshots/audit`: what the entries that have every label the query
names (as in a listing) rest on. Statuses come from the same axiom lists
as `dirty`: the build's report, or the kernel re-check once a module is
verified, so a trusted audit has no `rejected` or `sorry` and
`unverified_modules` 0. Whether an assumption is reasonable is for review.

assumptions.description:
The assumptions what the entries declare uses, by name, wherever they
are declared.

SnapshotDependents.description:
`GET /snapshots/{entry}/dependents`: the entries on every module that
imports the entry's module, directly or through others, parents first: by
level, where a module that imports it is at level 1 and one that imports
that at 2, by its longest chain, then oldest first. With `label=key:value`
filters, as in a listing, only the entries with every label.

reason.description: Why the re-check failed, e.g. the kernel's error or a timeout.

dirty.description:
See the snapshot API: the module depends on `sorry` or other axioms
outside the allowed list.

entries.description: The query's entries on the module, newest first, at most 10.

verified.description: The module and everything it imports passed the kernel re-check.

created.description: When the entry was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

replaces.description: The entry this one replaced, if it was created to.

SnapshotList.description:
`GET /snapshots`: the version's entries, newest first, that have every
label the query names as `label=key:value` (split on the first `:`; up to
64 filters), at most `limit` of them (1 to 1000, default 100). Keep
requesting with `next` as `after` while a page has it.

next.description:
Where the next page starts, if this page is full. The page after it
may be empty.

SnapshotRequest.description:
`POST /snapshots`: checks code like `/check` and, if Lean accepts it,
keeps it as a module that later code can import, with a new entry that
holds the module. Code that is already kept gets a new entry on its
module without being built again.

key.description:
Makes the create safe to retry: while an entry made with this key
exists, a create with it on the same code returns that entry as it is,
instead of adding another; on other code it is a `bad_request`. Such a
replay ignores the request's other fields, `labels` and `verify`
included, so it can be `verified: false` with no error after
`verify: true`. Creates that keep nothing don't use the key up, and
deleting the entry frees it. See [`check_key`](crate::labels::check_key)
for the rules.

labels.description:
The new entry's labels; see [`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels)
for the rules.

replaces.description:
The entry this code replaces, e.g. the skeleton a proof fills in. The
code is kept only if it still declares everything that entry's module
declares, each the same kind of declaration with the same type and,
for definitions, the same value, and adds no assumptions (`axiom`s,
its own or a newly imported snapshot's); it may add other declarations
and imports. If it no longer builds on
a snapshot that module does, what the module's declarations use from
there must be unchanged in what the code builds on now. Otherwise
nothing is kept and `result.reasons` lists the changes. The new entry
records the link.

timeout.description:
Lean's time limit in seconds, for building the module including its
imports.

verify.description:
Whether to re-check the code through the kernel. `true` also re-checks
its imports, so the result ends [`verified`](SnapshotResponse::verified)
or has an error, except on a [`key`](Self::key) replay. `false` never
re-checks. By default, only code that uses macros, its own or an
import's, is re-checked.

dirty.description:
Kept although a declaration uses `sorry` or another axiom outside the
allowed list; `result.reasons` says which.

entry.description:
The entry, which the other snapshot endpoints take: the one this create
added, or on a [`key`](SnapshotRequest::key) replay the one the key is
on. It keeps the module until it is deleted. Absent when nothing new
was kept: the code was not kept, it changed what the entry it
[`replaces`](SnapshotRequest::replaces) states (`result.reasons` says
how), or `verify: true` found it kept but failing the re-check. For
code that was already kept, `snapshot` and `header` are then set.

header.description:
The header to start code on top of this snapshot with: this code's
imports with its snapshots replaced by the new one. Code with exactly
this header reuses the Lean process the snapshot's builder keeps warm.

replaces.description: The entry it replaces, if the request named one.

result.description:
The check, as for `/check`. It has no `sorries`, and `time` includes
importing the module's imports.

snapshot.description:
The module to import, e.g. `PisaSnap.s1a2b…`, shared by every entry on
the same code. Absent when the code was not kept: Lean reported errors,
or the check could not complete.

status.description:
The worst status among the module's declarations: `dirty` unless
`proved`.

verified.description:
This snapshot and everything it imports have passed the kernel
re-check.

version.description: The worker pool version the snapshot belongs to.

SnapshotScope.description:
Which snapshot modules a query searches: `"none"`, `"all"`, or
`{"labels": {"k": "v"}}`, the modules of the entries that have every label.

SnapshotSummary.description:
An entry in a listing: as [`SnapshotInfo`], without the code and the check
result.

created.description: When the entry was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

SnapshotVerified.description:
`POST /snapshots/{entry}/verify`: re-checks the entry's module and
everything it imports through the kernel, imports first, skipping what
already passed. A module that fails stops the run and stays usable, marked
as not verified. `verified` and `dirty` belong to the module, so every
entry on it shows the result.

checked.description: The modules this run re-checked and passed, in order.

dirty.description: As in [`SnapshotResponse::dirty`], from the re-check if it got this far.

failure.description: The module that failed, if one did.

StartRequest.description:
`POST /sessions`: runs code containing `sorry`; each `sorry` becomes a
proof state that tactics can be applied to.

code.description: Code with `sorry`s, each of which becomes a state.

pos.description: Where the `sorry` is in the code.

TacticInfo.description: One run of a tactic, with the goals before and after it.

goals_after.description:
The goals left after it ran. A tactic that failed, such as an
alternative `first` dropped, leaves them as they were before.

TacticRequest.description: `POST /states/{state}/tactic`. A failing tactic is a 422 with kind `lean`.

complete.description:
No goals remain for this state's `sorry`. This says nothing about the
rest of the proof; check the assembled proof with the session check.

state.description: The new state. Earlier states stay valid, so a session is a tree.

TermInfo.description: A term written in the code, and the type Lean expected it to have.

expr.description: The term as Lean elaborated it.

info.description: Checks Lean code, runs proof sessions, keeps snapshots and searches declarations. Errors are `{error: {kind, message}}`, with a status that follows the kind. `/v1/*` is a 404 on a server without search.
info.title: pisa

post.description: Checks code against the version's Lean and imports. The verdict is `ok`; what Lean, the policy or a limit reported is in-band, in `error`, `messages` and `reasons`.
